result.title: Shift by Analogy for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning
result.summary: Compositional zero-shot learning recognizes attribute-object pairs absent from training. An unseen pair has a semantic description but lacks an observed visual reference. We propose Shift by Analogy (SBA) to make unseen compositions visually seen through a shift-then-match process. Its core add-subtract-add rule transfers an attribute change between two seen image-text residuals on a source object to a reference residual on the target object. This shifts the target's own text feature toward its visual center; learned refinement produces a proxy for matching query images. During training, each target is excluded from its supports, and recognition is learned using references constructed from other pairs. An analogy library and same-object attention extend this construction across candidates, while joint learning integrates proxy matching with semantic and primitive evidence. Visual-center analysis confirms substantially improved correspondence for unseen compositions. Experiments across three standard benchmarks show that SBA consistently outperforms strong CZSL baselines under both closed- and open-world evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Shift by Analogy，用「加减加」残差规则把已见图像-文本对上的属性变化迁移到目标物体的参考残差，将目标文本特征移向其视觉中心，再经学习精炼得到可匹配查询图像的代理特征，用于组合零样本识别，并结合语义与原始特征证据联合学习。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作并非研究 LVR 推理，但其用类比残差构造未见组合的视觉代理表示、训练时把目标排除在支持集外，可能为 latent 视觉证据构造与留一监督提供可核查线索。
